brief.title: Recurring methane, south Caspian site near Krasnovodsk
brief.place: Arid desert near Krasnovodsk, Turkmenistan, with linear infrastructure visible.
observations: EMIT looked at this site 24 times from 2022-08-15 to 2025-08-20.
NASA outlined methane plumes here on 4 dates (2023-06-20, 2023-10-09, 2024-08-12, 2024-10-05), with a peak of 4,096 ppm·m and a rate of 2,567.3 kg/h on 2024-10-05.
EMIT's own passes since 2025-01-01 show 4 candidates on 4 separate dates, with peaks of 1,916.0, 4,325.9, 9,144.0, and 4,353.6 ppm·m.
The strongest candidate on 2025-08-01 had 1,346 pixels at or above 1,000 ppm·m and 1,162 pixels above 3x uncertainty.
TROPOMI recorded a 122.9 ppb anomaly over this site in the 14 days to 2026-09-23, the highest of all watch areas scanned.
gaps: NASA's plume product is nearly empty after 2024, so passes since late 2024 have not been independently outlined.
EMIT only observes on its orbital passes and cannot provide continuous monitoring.
No wind-based flux estimates are available for the 2025 candidate passes.
Sentinel-2 imagery shows structures but cannot identify the specific source of methane enhancement.
brief.next_collection: A dedicated EMIT overpass or airborne survey over the Krasnovodsk site would confirm recurrence and provide a flux estimate.

explanations.label: Routine venting
explanations.next_check: Repeated enhancement on multiple dates without gaps would support this; ground inspection could confirm or rule it out.

explanations.label: Equipment failure or leak
explanations.next_check: A sudden increase in peak ppm·m or a change in plume location relative to prior passes would indicate this.

explanations.label: Unlit or malfunctioning flare
explanations.next_check: Night-time VIIRS thermal data showing no persistent heat source would help rule this out.

explanations.label: Maintenance blowdown
explanations.next_check: Enhancement on 4 separate dates spanning months is inconsistent with a single blowdown; aircraft passes would clarify.

explanations.label: Non-oil-and-gas source (landfill, coal, agriculture)
explanations.next_check: Sentinel-2 shows arid terrain with no wetlands or agriculture; a ground survey would confirm absence of biogenic sources.

**Methane Watch brief: Recurring methane, south Caspian site near Krasnovodsk** (draft `brief-20260925T203453-44f54b`, not filed)

Site: Arid desert near Krasnovodsk, Turkmenistan, with linear infrastructure visible. (39.4741, 53.6435), watch area south caspian
Looks: EMIT looked 24 times; 4 of 4 recent passes read are candidates.

- EMIT looked at this site 24 times from 2022-08-15 to 2025-08-20.
- NASA outlined methane plumes here on 4 dates (2023-06-20, 2023-10-09, 2024-08-12, 2024-10-05), with a peak of 4,096 ppm·m and a rate of 2,567.3 kg/h on 2024-10-05.
- EMIT's own passes since 2025-01-01 show 4 candidates on 4 separate dates, with peaks of 1,916.0, 4,325.9, 9,144.0, and 4,353.6 ppm·m.
- The strongest candidate on 2025-08-01 had 1,346 pixels at or above 1,000 ppm·m and 1,162 pixels above 3x uncertainty.
- TROPOMI recorded a 122.9 ppb anomaly over this site in the 14 days to 2026-09-23, the highest of all watch areas scanned.

| Hypothesis (unconfirmed) | Assessment | What would confirm or rule it out |
|---|---|---|
| Routine venting | possible | Repeated enhancement on multiple dates without gaps would support this; ground inspection could confirm or rule it out. |
| Equipment failure or leak | possible | A sudden increase in peak ppm·m or a change in plume location relative to prior passes would indicate this. |
| Unlit or malfunctioning flare | possible | Night-time VIIRS thermal data showing no persistent heat source would help rule this out. |
| Maintenance blowdown | less likely | Enhancement on 4 separate dates spanning months is inconsistent with a single blowdown; aircraft passes would clarify. |
| Non-oil-and-gas source (landfill, coal, agriculture) | less likely | Sentinel-2 shows arid terrain with no wetlands or agriculture; a ground survey would confirm absence of biogenic sources. |

Confidence that methane recurs at this site: high. Confidence in any single explanation: low without a ground or aircraft check.
Gaps: NASA's plume product is nearly empty after 2024, so passes since late 2024 have not been independently outlined.; EMIT only observes on its orbital passes and cannot provide continuous monitoring.; No wind-based flux estimates are available for the 2025 candidate passes.; Sentinel-2 imagery shows structures but cannot identify the specific source of methane enhancement..
Next collection: A dedicated EMIT overpass or airborne survey over the Krasnovodsk site would confirm recurrence and provide a flux estimate.
